exposure: postnatal nasogastric (NG) tube position (below or above the diaphragm)
cohort: The study included 464 neonates with left-sided isolated congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) who had prenatal diagnoses and were enrolled from the Japanese CDH Study Group database over 15 years.
finding: Postnatal nasogastric (NG) tube position below the diaphragm was a favorable prognostic factor, significantly associated with a higher 90-day survival rate, shorter mechanical ventilation, shorter hospitalization, and lower recurrence rate compared to a position above the diaphragm.
